pr_title: fix(release create): Handle latest flag value when updating the release after assets are uploaded
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/8201

With this PR, the `--latest` flag input will be accurately handled when updating the latest published release after assets are published. As an example, `--latest=false` will accurately mark that release as not latest after the assets are published.

To test, please checkout this branch and follow the testing instructions on the linked issue, following which that latest release should be marked as not latest:

- https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/8201
pr_comments: Thank you, @williammartin! Unfortunately, I had been backed up with a few other things that I couldn't follow through here earlier.

issue_context.title: `gh release create <tag> --latest=false` does not work when uploading assets
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

gh version 2.36.0 (2023-10-03)
When creating a release the option `--latest=false` has no effect if you upload assets in the same command.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior

```bash
# setup an existing github repository with an existing release
echo "hello" > hello.txt
git tag test-release
git push --tags

# create release (generate title for ease)
gh release create test-release --latest=false --generate-notes hello.txt
```

Observe in the releases that it is still marked as latest.

### Expected vs actual behavior

We expect this release (when other releases are present) to not be marked as the latest release when in fact it is being marked as the latest release.

### Logs
From running the above:
```
Enumerating objects: 3, done.
Counting objects: 100% (3/3), done.
Delta compression using up to 20 threads
Compressing objects: 100% (1/1), done.
Writing objects: 100% (2/2), 251 bytes | 251.00 KiB/s, done.
Total 2 (delta 0), reused 0 (delta 0), pack-reused 0
To https://github.com/MatBon01/test-actions.git
 * [new tag]         test-release -> test-release
https://github.com/MatBon01/test-actions/releases/tag/test-release
```

### Ideas
Looking at the code an asset is uploaded by creating a draft release. Perhaps the default behaviour when publishing a release from draft is to set it as latest and the overriding option is not being passed.
comments: @MatBon01 Thanks for writing in, I was able to confirm this bug and your hypothesis on what is happening here. When creating a release with assets the release is first created in draft mode and then published after the assets are uploaded. When published the `--latest` flag input is not being passed to that API request, and the default value is to make the published release the latest. It should be an easy enough fix though to make sure that parameter starts getting sent in the API request [here](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/fd8bbf0be5b590c61cf4fe1a67153b58a29a7579/pkg/cmd/release/create/create.go#L502). I am going to open this up for community contributions.

review_comments: @samcoe : should we consider [reusing the parameter preparation for creating the release](https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/7738b6187c80f128728aeba15fdba6bf62ec9e1b/pkg/cmd/release/create/create.go#L407-L427) since most of the parameters are reused for updating a release?
That's a good question. At the moment I don't think it is worth making the extra effort to extract that logic and make it re-usble. I don't have strong opinions though.
